The oracle `packages/operator-core/lib/startup/validate-active-routines.test.ts` requires, in the words of the engineer who shipped it:
  - should pass when all active routines target registered projects
  - should detect routines targeting unregistered harnesses
  - accepts reserved singleton and workspace hosts without registry lookups
  - should handle empty routine list
  - should detect empty slug as problematic
  - auto-deactivates an active routine targeting an unregistered harness, and logs AUTO-DEACTIVATED (not FATAL)
  - logs nothing for a routine a concurrent process already paused (UPDATE affects 0 rows)
  - never auto-heals a blank install_slug — keeps logging FATAL, issues no UPDATE
  - flags an active system: routine whose handler is NOT registered, and fails ok
  - passes when the handler IS registered
  - NEVER flags an inline loop fire — it bypasses the registry by dispatch precedence
  - still flags a system: routine that has an interval but NO bound owner (not a loop fire)
  - enforceActiveRoutines REPORTS an unregistered handler but issues no UPDATE

Restore `packages/operator-core/lib/console-spawn.ts` so its real test passes.

The oracle `packages/operator-core/lib/console-spawn.test.ts` requires, in the words of the engineer who shipped it:
  - returns code:501 (defer to the Tauri console_launch) on a Windows desktop host, even though process.platform is "linux" inside WSL
  - does NOT short-circuit to 501 on a real Linux desktop (isWindowsDesktopHost false)
  - allowDesktopBridge on a Windows desktop host relays via the bridge and returns ok (child:null)
  - surfaces a LOUD bridge failure (desktop shell closed / timeout) instead of ok-with-no-window
  - allowDesktopBridge is a no-op on a real Linux desktop — the server-side spawn stays in charge
  - a terminal client that dies nonzero inside the probe ⇒ LOUD error (no more ok+pid ghost windows)
  - a client killed by a signal inside the probe ⇒ LOUD error
  - a client that outlives the probe ⇒ ok with its pid
  - slugifies the label + stamps pid/time under the given dir
  - falls back to tmpdir when no dir given, and never yields an empty base name
  - falls back to bash -lc (no terminal emulator, no systemd-run) detached with a log fd, and reports ok+pid when the session outlives the probe
  - a psu that dies at boot inside the probe ⇒ LOUD error (not a false ok+pid)
  - EI-9748: installs a TERM trap ahead of the greeting so a cgroup-restart kill logs a diagnostic instead of dying silently
  - EI-9748 Route (A): when systemd-run is available on Linux, spawns via systemd-run --user --scope instead of plain bash — the cgroup escape
  - EI-9748 Route (A): falls back to plain bash on a platform/host without systemd-run (e.g. macOS)
  - picks systemd-run --user --scope --collect on Linux with systemd-run available
  - sanitizes the label into a safe systemd unit-name fragment
  - falls back to plain bash -lc when systemd-run is unavailable
  - falls back to plain bash -lc on a non-Linux platform even if hasSystemdRun somehow returns true
  - emits a slice for the UN-ENROLLED fallback, not just the enrolled path
  - still honours the caller-supplied slice when enrolment DID succeed
  - STRUCTURAL: every input that produces a scope produces a slice
  - adds no slice on the non-systemd fallback, where there is no scope to place
  - prepends a TERM trap that logs + exits 143, then runs the original oneliner unmodified
  - the trap body is syntactically balanced (single-quoted, no unescaped internal single-quotes)
  - cds, evals the greeting in a subshell, then execs an interactive login shell
  - always drops to the shell after the greeting and prints a failure banner for non-zero greetings
  - drops the sentinel + EXIT trap so the desktop side can detect shell exit
  - carries a command containing quotes as an escaped eval literal (no breakout, no mangle)
  - a quote-bearing greeting yields a one-liner bash can actually parse (bash -n)
  - executes a quoted greeting verbatim end-to-end (subshell eval round-trip)
  - a MALFORMED greeting (unbalanced quote) errors inside the subshell without killing the one-liner
  - preserves pipes / redirects / && in the arbitrary command
  - exports env vars with valid bash names and skips invalid ones
  - prepends PAPERCUSP_BIN_DIR ahead of PAPERCUSP_SCRIPTS_DIR on PATH
  - emits the OSC window-title prelude
  - happy path: spawns the DISPLAY-honoring emulator with env.DISPLAY = the override, WAYLAND_DISPLAY stripped, resolvedVia caller-override
  - dead/unprovisioned display socket ⇒ LOUD 412 before any spawn (no off-screen ghost)
  - no DISPLAY-honoring emulator installed ⇒ 500 naming the installable candidates (never a client-server fallback)
  - an unparseable override value ⇒ 400, not a silent seat spawn
  - default path (no override) is unchanged: seat resolution runs and reports its own resolvedVia
  - desktop session DETECTED ⇒ prefers the owner’s standard gnome-terminal over xterm
  - NO desktop session ⇒ prefers the reliable process-per-window xterm over gnome-terminal
  - default (no flag) is the no-session ordering — process-per-window first
  - desktop session DETECTED but only a process-per-window emulator installed ⇒ still uses it
  - NO session but only a client-server terminal installed ⇒ still falls back to it
  - an explicit $TERMINAL is still honored as-is, regardless of the preference flag
  - returns null when no known emulator is installed
  - a detected desktop session normally prefers client-server (gnome-terminal) — unchanged for a fresh launch
  - a RESUME launch (preferProcessPerWindow) forces process-per-window even WITH a detected desktop session
  - no desktop session already prefers process-per-window, regardless of the override
  - composed with pickLinuxTerminal: a resume on a desktop box picks xterm over gnome-terminal (the bug fix)
  - composed with pickLinuxTerminal: a FRESH launch on the same desktop box still picks the standard gnome-terminal
  - $TERMINAL=gnome-terminal must NOT hijack the override path (client-server: its window lands on the seat)
  - $TERMINAL naming a DISPLAY-honoring candidate is honored when on PATH (bash stands in as not-a-candidate)
  - formats a present id and elides a missing one
  - a bound scheme drives fg (OSC 10), bg (OSC 11) and cursor (OSC 12) — overriding the plan hash
  - without a scheme: no cursor OSC, and bg falls back to the per-plan hash
  - writes a one-shot .command that self-deletes then execs the login-shell one-liner
  - a quote-bearing greeting survives BOTH layers: the .command parses and its inner bash -lc payload parses
  - names a fresh .command per pid+timestamp under tmpDir
  - opens a FRESH instance (open -na) so every call is a new window
  - prefers iTerm when installed, else Terminal.app
  - carries the OSC color prelude into the .command (fleet colors work on Mac, no Rust port)
  - `open` exiting NON-ZERO ⇒ LOUD error, not a phantom ok (the GUI-less rig mac)
  - `open` killed by a signal ⇒ error
  - `open` exiting 0 ⇒ ok — an early exit is NORMAL on mac (open is a launcher, not the terminal)
  - a slow `open` that outlives the probe ⇒ ok (fail OPEN — never manufacture a failure)
  - `open` that never STARTS (spawn 'error', no 'exit') ⇒ error, NOT a fail-open ok
  - no GUI session (/dev/console owned by root) ⇒ error BEFORE spawning — the rig mac
  - `open` exits 0 but the .command is NEVER executed ⇒ error, not a phantom ok
  - the .command disappearing mid-wait ⇒ ok (a slow but genuine launch is not failed)
  - greeting-failure sentinel ⇒ error, even though the process is still alive
  - sentinel appearing LATE (after the early-exit probe) is still caught
  - a healthy member (no sentinel) ⇒ ok — never manufacture a failure
  - sentinel with status 0 is ALSO a dead member (the agent command ended at all)
  - root-owned /dev/console ⇒ no GUI session
  - user-owned /dev/console ⇒ GUI session
  - unreadable /dev/console ⇒ no GUI session (fail toward the path that RUNS)

  - the same root always maps to the same lock dir (cron-vs-manual still single-flights)

  - two roots contend only on their own lock end-to-end (acquire under root A never blocks root B)

  - defaults to console.error when no log fn is injected (does not throw)
  - keeps the self-watchdog at the 3h long-run floor
  - does nothing before the deadline

Restore `packages/operator-core/lib/events/await/pattern.ts` so its real test passes.

The oracle `packages/operator-core/lib/events/await/pattern.test.ts` requires, in the words of the engineer who shipped it:
  - flags globs and @macros; exact keys are not patterns
  - @plan:<slug> → plan-item:done:<slug>:* (grounded on the catalog scheme)
  - @fleet:<slug> → fleet:*:<slug>
  - passes a raw glob or exact key through unchanged
  - throws loudly on an unknown macro (a typo must not store a dead key)
  - compiles to an anchored matches regex with * → .* and literals escaped
  - a glob matches every key in its family, and only that family
  - is anchored — a prefix glob does NOT match a longer unrelated key
  - @plan macro matches any item finishing in that plan (the headline use case)
  - @fleet macro matches any fleet event for the slug
  - a mid-key wildcard matches across one segment
  - an exact (non-pattern) key degrades to string equality
  - a null/undefined filter always matches (no predicate registered)
  - evaluates the $-free OperatorTest vocabulary (lt/gte/…) against a payload field
  - supports the all/any/not combinators (same vocabulary as an ECA rule when)
  - a payload missing the tested field fails the predicate rather than throwing
  - a non-object filter (string/number/array) is rejected up front, never vacuously true
  - a malformed operand inside an otherwise-valid filter degrades to false rather than throwing
  - anchors on the literal segment before the first wildcard
  - returns no prefix when the glob leads with a wildcard, so a caller cannot turn it into an unbounded scan
  - trims back to a whole segment rather than cutting mid-segment
  - passes an exact (wildcard-free) key through whole
  - is defensive about a non-string key, like its siblings on the emit path
  - the incident glob really does cross pipelines — the regression this exists to disclose
  - accepts an anchored glob
  - rejects a wildcard-only / near-empty pattern that would wake-storm
